title: The Cornerstone
lead: The stone that holds a building's corner and sets its lines. The prophets and psalms use it for God's secure foundation in Zion, and the New Testament for Christ, the stone the builders rejected (Psalm 118:22; Isaiah 28:16; 1 Peter 2:6–8).

sections.b:
In ancient building, the cornerstone was laid first and fixed the lines of the walls. Job hears God ask, about the founding of the earth, "Who set down its corner stone" (Job 38:6). Isaiah uses stone imagery in two directions: the LORD is "a stone that people strike their foot on" for those who refuse him (Isaiah 8:14), and he lays in Zion a tested stone, "a cornerstone of great worth" (Isaiah 28:16), for those who trust. Psalm 118:22 sings of "a stone that the builders threw out" that "has become the head of the corner," and Zechariah sees the top stone brought out with shouts of grace (Zechariah 4:7).

The Qumran community applied Isaiah 28:16 to its own council, "the tested wall, the precious cornerstone" (1QS VIII, 7–8). Jesus quotes Psalm 118:22 of himself (Matthew 21:42), Peter repeats it before the council (Acts 4:11), and the letters gather the stone texts together: Romans 9:33 joins Isaiah 28:16 with Isaiah 8:14, Ephesians 2:20 calls Christ the cornerstone of a temple built from Jews and Gentiles, and 1 Peter 2:4–8 calls believers "living stones" built on him.
